The new WRF will replace the existing WWTP with a membrane bioreactor (MBR) wastewater treatment facility that will produce tertiary treated effluent that exceeds secondary standards for discharge.

Tertiary treated effluent from the outfall balancing tank will be pumped through an outfall disinfection chlorine contact pipeline and will then be dechlorinated by sodium bisulfite injection prior to discharge through the ocean outfall.

A concrete tank, called the SAFE settling basin, will capture and equalize the wet weather flows prior to entering the SAFE filter system... effluent will fill the SAFE settling basin, which will provide sedimentation treatment, until it passes over a weir and flows to the SAFE filter system for filtration treatment.

Primary treated effluent from the SAFE filter system will then be routed to the outfall balancing tank where it will be blended with tertiary-treated MBR effluent and pumped by the outfall pump station to the outfall disinfection pipeline contactor and then the ocean outfall.

RO concentrate will also be diverted directly to the RO concentrate disinfection contact pipeline for chlorination prior to commingling with the outfall disinfection contact pipeline upstream of the dechlorination injection point.

The sludge holding tanks will receive, store, and aerate activated sludge wasted from the BNR MBR process. The holding tanks will consist of a two cell design, with each zone including mixers and bubble diffusers.
The sludge dewatering system will pump waste sludge from the sludge holding tanks, or directly from the MBR system, and dewatered by a belt filter press with a polymer storage and feed system.
Dewatered biosolids will be transported offsite for beneficial use or landfill.
